sections.history: Tiruneelakudi lies on the northern bank of the Nattaru river, about 13–15 km from Kumbakonam on the Kumbakonam–Karaikal road, in Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Appar (Tirunavukkarasar) and Sambandar. The structural temple is of the early Chola period, with later additions by the Pandyas and Vijayanagara rulers.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Neelakandeswarar — locally also Chozheeswaramudaiyar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Oppilamulaiyal (Anupamasthani) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The Navagraha shrine stands in the north-eastern corner, and devotees perform remedial worship to the lord for relief from the planet Rahu.
sections.legends: Shiva is praised here as Neelakandeswarar, the blue-throated lord who drank the halahala poison of the churned ocean; the goddess is Oppilamulaiyal, 'she beyond compare.' The shrine is counted among the places of parihara for Rahu, one of the shadow planets, and the lord is besought here to turn aside the planet's adverse aspect. The fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, and special worship on the days reckoned auspicious for Rahu parihara. Pilgrims of the Kumbakonam country include Tiruneelakudi among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruneelakudi the pilgrim comes to the blue-throated lord's shrine by the Nattaru. Before Neelakandeswarar and Oppilamulaiyal, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the Kumbakonam delta, and the hope of the Rahu parihara for which the shrine is sought.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruneelakudi lies about 13–15 km from Kumbakonam on the Kumbakonam–Karaikal road, on the northern bank of the Nattaru, in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
